proposedOverrides.name: Peru
proposedOverrides.summary: Peru proclaimed independence in 1821, decades before this map record begins. The republic encompasses coastal, Andean and Amazonian communities whose histories extend far beyond the state. Its story includes railways and libraries, living textile and pottery knowledge, and the difficult work of confronting political violence.

proposedOverrides.name: Louisiana
proposedOverrides.summary: Colonial Louisiana connected Gulf settlements with the Mississippi valley through French claims, trade and settlement. Indigenous peoples, Africans and Europeans shaped its life under deeply unequal conditions. This map shows a limited Gulf-area slice; neither its outline nor its 1715 to 1783 dates represents the entire colonial territory or history.

proposedOverrides.name: Rupert’s Land
proposedOverrides.summary: Rupert’s Land was the Hudson’s Bay Company’s claimed trading territory in the Hudson Bay watershed, established by an English charter in 1670. Indigenous nations lived and governed there. The map’s 1783 to 1815 slice is shorter than the company jurisdiction’s history. Its imported outline extends beyond that watershed and remains unverified.

proposedOverrides.name: British Guiana
proposedOverrides.summary: British Guiana was formed in 1831 by joining British-controlled Demerara-Essequibo and Berbice, in present-day Guyana. Its earlier history involved Dutch colonies. The imported 1783 to 1914 dates are not the colony’s lifespan, and the associated outline chiefly covers neighbouring Suriname, so it is not an accurate map of this colony.

batchIdentityNotes.assessment: Modern republic. Imported 1878 start is map coverage, not 1821 independence. Decoded earliest shape includes southern coastal territory before the War of the Pacific; do not compare it uncritically to present boundaries. Narrative is distinct from the Inca Empire and Viceroyalty of Peru.

The shape follows the eastern part of New Guinea and adjacent islands, resembling the footprint of a much later nation. No united Papua New Guinea state existed in 1715. Card distinguishes local societies, nineteenth-century colonial divisions, joint twentieth-century administration and 1975 independence. Broad island geometry cannot establish the extent of any particular Indigenous community.

Imported 1715 to 1783 coverage is not French Louisiana’s lifespan. Decoded polygon is only a Gulf strip from 30.14N to 31.85N; it omits the huge Mississippi basin and even New Orleans at about 29.95N. Card explicitly acknowledges limited extent and distinguishes French, Spanish and US transitions. No geometry correction performed.

Company claim to Hudson Bay watershed, not a nation or complete consensual sovereignty. Imported 1783 to 1815 is a slice of 1670 to 1870 jurisdiction. Decoded extent is substantially overbroad, reaching about 141W and 39.82N; it cannot be accepted as an accurate watershed boundary. Indigenous and Métis political continuity retained.

Late British colonial slice of 1836 to 1901 South Australia, distinct from federal Australia. Decoded outline begins only around 24.94S, omitting the Northern Territory then administered by the colony; its 38.38S southern extreme also needs boundary review. Narrative acknowledges Northern Territory administration without implying whole-colony geometry is accurate.

Late British colony, 1878 to 1900 map coverage inside 1829 to 1901 historical phase. Decoded western continental extent supports identity; full boundary precision unverified. Federation in 1901 transformed the colony into a state; a post-federation 1903 pipeline completion is explicitly dated.

Modern Greenland geographic identity supported by decoded island extent. Start 1960 is map coverage, between 1953 incorporation into the Danish realm and 1979 Home Rule. Card distinguishes expanded 2009 self-government and continuing Inuit communities; no claim of present sovereign independence.

MAJOR UNRESOLVED IDENTITY/GEOMETRY CONFLICT. Earliest polygon extends 58.58W to 53.84W and chiefly covers Suriname, not the historical British Guiana administration centred on Demerara/Essequibo/Berbice. 1783 also predates the unified colony created in 1831; 1914 is not the 1966 independence date. Narrative follows the indexed label and explicitly warns about its outline. Do not silently count this geometry as corrected; root must choose publication treatment. No runtime or geometry changes made.
